Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: English Bluff is the west shore of Tsawwassen, in the City of Delta, running along English Bluff Road from 12 Avenue south to 1 Avenue and the Strait of Georgia shore, around English Bluff Elementary School at 402 English Bluff Road.

The defining landmarks are Fred Gingell Park, 253 English Bluff Rd (picnic tables, trails, viewpoint, and stairs from the upper park down to the beach), and Diefenbaker Park, 5579 1 Ave (playgrounds, trails, viewpoint, washrooms, water park).

Transit on the bluff itself is community-shuttle scale: route 604 English Bluff / Bridgeport Station runs via 56 Street, 16 Avenue, Beach Grove Road, 12 Avenue, English Bluff Road and 1 Avenue with peak service to Bridgeport Station, and the 614 English Bluff shuttle loops via 1 Avenue, English Bluff Road and 12 Avenue from South Delta Exchange.

Where condo stock concentrates: it does not concentrate here at all. The Delta Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 8400, focuses Tsawwassen growth on the Urban Centre, the 56 Street corridor, Southlands and Tsawwassen Springs — all outside English Bluff.

Development Permit Area SD2 — the rule that defines this shore: OCP Bylaw No. 8400 names "SD2 English Bluff (Tsawwassen Escarpment)," Category "b" (protection of development from hazardous conditions): the waterfront area is subject to mud flows, debris flows, erosion, land slip and subsidence, the ocean-frontage slopes are subject to erosion, and existing vegetation and tree cover on the slopes must be protected.
The OCP deliberately steers growth away from this shore. Bylaw No. 8400 focuses Tsawwassen growth on the Urban Centre, the 56 Street corridor, Southlands and Tsawwassen Springs.

The flood covenant runs with the land. SD2's guidelines require a restrictive covenant acknowledging the land may be subject to flooding — it will show on title and bind the next owner, which is why bluff listings have to be read title-first.

The stairs at Fred Gingell Park are the public beach access for the upper bluff — a City report states stairs run from the upper park at 253 English Bluff Rd down to the beach, which matters to homes on the landward side with no stairs of their own.

Delta's flood system is municipal-scale, and the bluff is its edge case: the City operates and maintains over 63 km of flood protection infrastructure, 31 drainage pump stations and approximately 538 km of drainage infrastructure — but SD2 lots carry site-specific engineer-set conditions on top of that system.

The RS3 lot standard explains why there is no condo product to find: a 4,000 m² minimum subdivision lot area (estate-scale by Delta standards, where the wider Bylaw 7600 ladder starts at RS7's 335 m²) keeps this shore in large detached lots.

Health care is inland: Delta Hospital, 5800 Mountain View Boulevard in Ladner, is the nearest hospital, and Fraser Health lists a South Delta After-Hours Urgent and Primary Care Centre at 1826-4949 Canoe Pass Way in Tsawwassen.

The SnapStats FVR September 2026 report contains no English Bluff, Tsawwassen or South Delta section — its only Delta section is North Delta, and South Delta is not covered by SnapStats at all — so any "English Bluff median townhouse price" quoted from that source does not exist.

blocks.text: Lots and land in English Bluff
What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple estate lots — the only form: The confirmed stock is freehold single detached housing under the RS zones along English Bluff Road and its side streets, including waterfront and bluff-top lots on the Strait of Georgia shore. The RS3 zone sheet that fits this shore describes a zone for single detached housing in the vicinity of Georgia Strait, with a minimum subdivision lot area of 4,000 m², lot width 30 m and average lot depth 30 m — estate-scale lots by Delta standards, where the wider ladder runs from RS7 at 335 m² up to the 4,000 m² RS1/RS2/RS3 and RD2/RD3 standards, assigned parcel by parcel.

The lot does not include the beach: The foreshore below the natural boundary is Crown land administered through FrontCounter BC, and Delta states foreshore and water use is interjurisdictional (federal Fisheries Act, provincial Water Sustainability Act and Riparian Areas Regulation, flood protection requirements and Delta bylaws) — upland ownership alone does not grant foreshore use, stairs or docks.

The OCP's named Tsawwassen growth locations — Urban Centre, 56 Street corridor, Southlands, Tsawwassen Springs — are all outside English Bluff; they are documented AS plan direction, never as this sub-area's inventory.
A specific parcel's status is checked in the ALC's ALR Property and Map Finder and on title.
Servicing: the City operates and maintains over 63 km of flood protection infrastructure, 31 drainage pump stations and approximately 538 km of drainage infrastructure.

blocks.text: Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: Municipality: City of Delta. English Bluff is the west shore of Tsawwassen, and Tsawwassen is the Official Community Plan community area.

Where it sits (working geography): roughly the west shore of Tsawwassen along English Bluff Road, from 12 Avenue south to 1 Avenue and the Strait of Georgia shore, around English Bluff Elementary School at 402 English Bluff Road. Nearby areas: Beach Grove (north along the shore), Tsawwassen Central and Tsawwassen East (inland), Pebble Hill, and Boundary Bay / Point Roberts across the border to the south.

Landmarks are parks and the school, not complexes: Fred Gingell Park, 253 English Bluff Rd (picnic tables, trails, viewpoint, and stairs from the upper park down to the beach, per a City report), and Diefenbaker Park, 5579 1 Ave (picnic tables, playgrounds, trails, viewpoint, washrooms, water park). Recreation: South Delta Recreation Centre, 1720 56 St; Tsawwassen Library (Fraser Valley Regional Library), 1321A 56 St. Health: Delta Hospital, 5800 Mountain View Blvd, Ladner; a South Delta After-Hours Urgent and Primary Care Centre at 1826 – 4949 Canoe Pass Way.

Transit: route 604 English Bluff / Bridgeport Station runs via 56 Street, 16 Avenue, Beach Grove Road, 12 Avenue, English Bluff Road and 1 Avenue, with peak service to Bridgeport Station; the 614 English Bluff community shuttle loops via 1 Avenue, English Bluff Road and 12 Avenue from South Delta Exchange; route 603 Beach Grove also traverses English Bluff Road. Highway 17 also leads to the Tsawwassen Ferry Terminal, served by the 620 express.

Market numbers: none. SnapStats does not cover South Delta / Tsawwassen — the FVR September 2026 report contains no English Bluff, Tsawwassen or South Delta section, and North Delta figures were deliberately not substituted. Land has no SnapStats category in any case.

Hazard DPA SD2 — the defining rule set on this shore, in full: Development Permit Area SD2, "SD2 English Bluff (Tsawwassen Escarpment)", Category "b" (protection of development from hazardous conditions), covers this shore. The OCP states the waterfront area is subject to mud flows, debris flows, erosion, land slip and subsidence, and the ocean-frontage slopes are subject to erosion and require protection of existing vegetation and tree cover. Building rules: no building may sit with the underside of a wooden floor system, or the top of a concrete slab for habitation, business or storage of goods damageable by floodwaters, lower than the Flood Construction Level (unless a lesser elevation is set by the provincial ministry); no building within 7.5 m of the natural boundary of the sea or within 7.5 m of the inboard toe of any dike; the guidelines require a restrictive covenant acknowledging the land may be subject to flooding; and development affected by hazardous conditions is subject to conditions set by a suitably qualified Professional Engineer.

Strata block, governing no known English Bluff land stock: if a bare-land strata lot were ever the purchase, the BC block would apply to the LOT — Form B (Strata Property Act s. 59) within 7 days, max $35 plus up to 25¢/page; depreciation reports every five years for stratas with five or more lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 and Regulation 7.01, May 1, 2023 exemptions); a "45+" listing line is not a valid age bylaw.
Growth is deliberately directed away from this shore. The OCP focuses Tsawwassen growth on the Urban Centre, the 56 Street corridor, Southlands and Tsawwassen Springs — all outside English Bluff.

The covenant is part of the land, not paperwork trivia. SD2's required restrictive covenant acknowledging flood risk registers on title and runs with the lot — a buyer inherits it, and a resale buyer will find it in the same title search.

faq.a: Inland, in the two clusters: the 56 Street / 12 Avenue town-centre buildings in Tsawwassen Central, and Tsawwassen Springs on Springs Boulevard in Tsawwassen North. The OCP itself focuses Tsawwassen growth on the Urban Centre, the 56 Street corridor, Southlands and Tsawwassen Springs — not on the bluff.
faq.q: Where do English Bluff downsizers actually buy a condo?

faq.a: Delta's SSMUH bylaws (Nos. 8394 and 8395, adopted Jun 24, 2024) allow up to four units on single-detached and duplex lots city-wide, but on this shore the SD2 hazard permit area sits on top of that permission, with a Professional Engineer's conditions, a Flood Construction Level and a registered flood covenant.
faq.q: Could a bluff lot be split into a small strata or multiplex instead?

faq.a: No. The foreshore below the natural boundary is Crown land administered through FrontCounter BC, and Delta notes foreshore use is interjurisdictional — upland ownership does not include the beach below the natural boundary.
faq.q: Is the beach in front of a waterfront house private?

faq.a: Inland, in the clusters: the 56 Street / 12 Avenue town-centre buildings in Tsawwassen Central and Tsawwassen Springs on Springs Boulevard in Tsawwassen North. The OCP itself focuses Tsawwassen growth on the Urban Centre, the 56 Street corridor, Southlands and Tsawwassen Springs — not on the bluff.
faq.q: Where do English Bluff downsizers actually buy a townhouse or condo?

faq.a: No — both are apartment-condo buildings in Tsawwassen Central (elevator, underground parking, MLS Apartment/Condo classification), known 55+ in the 55+ run. They are the nearest 55+ ownership, but they are not townhouse form and not in English Bluff.
faq.q: Are The Lexington and Tsawwassen Greene townhomes I could consider nearby?

faq.a: No. That product is on Tsawwassen First Nation lands and is leasehold, not freehold strata or fee-simple: there is no Form B, no strata depreciation report, and the land tenure itself is the diligence item.
faq.q: What about the townhomes at Tsawwassen Landing / Boardwalk — are they the same kind of purchase?

faq.a: The confirmed stock is freehold detached homes on estate-scale lots (RS3 minimum 4,000 m²), and condos and townhomes inside English Bluff are few or none confirmed.
faq.q: Is there a duplex or half duplex I can buy in English Bluff?

faq.a: The city-wide SSMUH permission (up to four units on single-detached and duplex lots) applies on paper, but on this shore the SD2 hazard conditions sit on top of it: A Professional Engineer's conditions, the Flood Construction Level, 7.5 m setbacks from the natural boundary of the sea, and a registered restrictive covenant.
faq.q: Delta allows four units on a duplex lot — can I build a duplex on the bluff?

faq.a: Not the upland owner: The foreshore below the natural boundary is Crown land, and Delta notes foreshore use is interjurisdictional — do not market private beach ownership, stairs or docks without checking tenure.
faq.q: Who owns the beach below a waterfront house?

faq.a: The SD2 justification requires protection of existing vegetation and tree cover on the ocean-frontage slopes — tree removal for a view can need approvals and can affect the slope itself.
faq.q: Can I clear the slope trees for a better view?
